title: Support pipeline autopatcher: transform runbooks into guarded tasklets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'autopatcher' service that ingests runbook artifacts and emits guarded, idempotent tasklets that can be executed via the Console or API. The goal is to reduce mean time to resolution for common support flows while preserving safety (RBAC, audit, dry-run). This ticket wires the autopatcher into the runbook registry, adds a validation layer, and surfaces an operator preview in the Console's Support > Quick Actions panel.
acceptance_criteria: Autopatcher can parse at least three canonical runbook formats (markdown steps, playlet JSON, and existing task DSL) and produce normalized tasklets
Each patched tasklet includes metadata for RBAC, estimated duration, and revert instructions
Console UI shows a preview with dry-run output and a one-click 'create gated run' flow
Audit log entries emitted for every patched-tasklet creation and subsequent execution attempts
E2E smoke test exercising a patched shortflow (create -> dry-run -> gated execute) passes in CI
steps: design: finalize mapping of runbook primitives to tasklet operations (operators/steps/guards)
backend: implement parser adapters and normalization pipeline (stateless service behind ops-gateway)
backend: implement guard/enforcer middleware (RBAC checks, timeouts, revert hooks)
console: preview modal and dry-run log renderer plus gated-execute button
qa: add CI e2e test and a simulated incident harness
security: run threat model and KMS access review; get signoff
decision_log: 2026-02-12 — Chose a stateless, idempotent output format (tasklet JSON) over embedding exec scripts to simplify auditing and rollback
2026-02-18 — Decided to implement dry-run semantics that simulate actions using a sandbox layer rather than mocking responses, since earlier mocks missed latency/errors
2026-02-25 — Agreed on RBAC model: authoring requires 'runbook.editor', execution gating requires 'runbook.executor' and a two-step approval for high-impact tasklets
risks: Over-eager automatic conversion could produce non-idempotent steps; mitigated by requiring explicit revert hooks or rejecting ambiguous primitives
Console exposure may lead to accidental runs; mitigated via gated execute + two-step approval + rate limits
Parser coverage gaps for proprietary runbook formats — initial rollout will be opt-in per team
comments: 2026-02-11 — Asha Patel: Drafted initial spec and prototype parser for markdown runbooks. Found ~8 step patterns in Support's top-50 tickets.
2026-02-16 — Sofia Martinez (Design): Added UX mockups for preview modal; highlighted need to show estimated cost and required permissions up front.

2026-03-10 — QA: added CI smoke test that runs dry-run on a sample shortflow and asserts no network side effects; flaky on first run — increased timeout and stabilized.
2026-03-13 — PM (Noah Kim): Recommend soft launch with Customer Success team and feature flag behind 'autopatcher-preview' for two weeks.
notes: Prototype uses a breadcrumbed normalization approach so future adapters can be added with minimal risk
Recommend follow-up EPIC to cover 'complex conditional branching' and 'external-system orchestration' which are out of scope here
Telemetry: track patched->executed conversion rate, dry-run to execution time, and errors surfaced during dry-run
